kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.

 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre

 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *

 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).

 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)

 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by

function.name: play_test
function.description: Run a game or web page from the workspace in a real browser and test it like a player. Returns uncaught errors, console errors, files that failed to load, visible text and a screenshot. Optional "actions" are inputs played in order: "click" (centre), "click X Y", "click Start Game" (a button by its text), "click #start" (CSS selector), "key ArrowLeft 500" (hold ms), "key Space", "tap Space 8 350" (8 quick presses 350 ms apart, for flapping or jumping games), "type hello", "mouse X Y", "wait 1000". After each input it says whether the screen changed, and it reports window.__game (state and score) for games built on the game kit. "Errors: none" does not mean the game works: read "What happened" and WATCH OUT. Run it after every change to a game and fix everything it reports. The user can play the same file in the Play tab.

function.name: game_recipe
function.description: Tested code to add a feature to a kit.js or kit3d.js game, in parts (top of game.js, init, update, and draw for 2D) to paste in with file_edit. It picks the 2D or 3D version for the game in the workspace. 2D recipes: "lives" (three lives with a short invincible blink after each hit, hearts drawn in the corner); "coins" (coins that appear around the level and score when the player touches them); "powerup" (a shield power-up that floats in now and then; touching it makes the player safe for 5 seconds); "sprite" (draw the player from a PNG made with make_sprite, with a walking or flapping animation from a sprite sheet); "chaser" (enemies that appear at the edges and move toward the player; touching one ends the round (or calls hurt() from the lives recipe)); "timer" (a countdown; when it reaches zero the round ends with "Time up!" and the score stays); "levels" (a level number that goes up every 10 points, makes things faster and shows a "Level N" banner); "background" (a scrolling starfield or snowfall behind everything (draw it first in draw())). 3D recipes: "lives" (three lives with a blinking safe time after each hit; call hurt() where the game used to end the round); "coins" (spinning coins around the player that score when touched; new ones keep appearing); "chaser" (enemies (assets/enemy.glb, a red ball until it exists) that appear around the player and chase it; touching one calls hurt() from the lives recipe, or ends the round); "shooting" (click, Enter or F fires balls the way the player faces; they defeat chasers (from the chaser recipe) and score); "moving_platforms" (platforms that slide and bob; the player rides them (they are solid)); "timer" (a countdown on screen; at zero the round ends with "Time up!" and the score stays); "powerup" (a speed-boost gem appears now and then; touching it makes boostTime > 0 for 5 seconds (multiply the speed by boostTime > 0 ? 1.8 : 1)); "levels" (a level number that goes up every 10 points with a sound; multiply speeds by levelSpeed() to make it harder); "scenery" (copies of a model made with make_model (trees, houses, rocks) placed around the world as solid scenery); "gather" (survival gathering: trees and rocks around the world; press F, Enter or click next to one to hit it for wood or stone, shown in an inventory line (inv.wood, inv.stone)); "craft" (crafting for the gather recipe: press 1 for a hatchet (5 wood, doubles wood) and 2 for a pickaxe (3 wood + 5 stone, doubles stone); a line shows the recipes and what you have); "build" (building for the gather recipe: press B to place a wooden wall in front of the player (2 wood) and V for a stone one (2 stone); walls are solid); "hunger" (survival needs: health and hunger that run down; berry bushes to eat from (F, Enter or click next to one); starving hurts and at 0 health the round ends); "daynight" (a day and night cycle (one day is 90 seconds): the sky and lights darken at night; g.night is true at night, so other code can spawn more enemies then).

function.name: make_sprite
function.description: Draw pixel-art and save it as a PNG for a 2D game. "pixels" is a list of strings, one per row; each character is one pixel and "." is transparent. "palette" maps each character to a color ("#rrggbb" or a name like red, yellow). "scale" makes each pixel bigger (default 4). For animation give "frames" (a list of pixel lists, same size) to get a sprite sheet with frames side by side. Example bird 8x6: {"path":"assets/bird.png","pixels":["..YYYY..",".YYYYWB.","YYYYYYOO","OYYYYYY.",".YYYYY..","..Y..Y.."],"palette":{"Y":"#ffd23f","W":"white","B":"black","O":"orange"}}. Draw it with Kit.image("assets/bird.png") and Kit.drawImage.

frames.description: several pixel grids for an animation sheet

function.name: make_model
function.description: Build a low-poly 3D model (.glb, loads with three.js GLTFLoader) out of simple shapes. Shapes: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, wedge, torus. Each part: {"shape", "size": [width, height, depth] (the box the shape fills), "position": [x, y, z] (its centre), "on": "<name of an earlier part>" to rest it on top of that part (then x and z are offsets from that part's centre and y is ignored), "rotation": [x, y, z] degrees, "color": "#rrggbb", optional "name", "flat": true for a faceted look, "roughness", "metalness", "emissive": "#rrggbb", "opacity", "segments"}. Units are metres and y is up; put the model's base at y = 0 so it stands on the ground. Wedge is a ramp sloping down toward +z. Torus lies flat; size [outer width, tube thickness, outer depth]. Example: a tree is a "cylinder" trunk {"size":[0.3,1.2,0.3],"position":[0,0.6,0],"color":"#8b5a2b"} and a "cone" top {"size":[1.4,1.8,1.4],"position":[0,2.1,0],"color":"#3f8f3a","flat":true,"segments":7}.

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

function.name: make_model
function.description: Build a low-poly 3D model (.glb, loads with three.js GLTFLoader) out of simple shapes. Shapes: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, wedge, torus. Each part: {"shape", "size": [width, height, depth] (the box the shape fills), "position": [x, y, z] (its centre), "on": "<name of an earlier part>" to rest it on top of that part (then x and z are offsets from that part's centre and y is ignored), "rotation": [x, y, z] degrees, "color": "#rrggbb", optional "name", "flat": true for a faceted look, "roughness", "metalness", "emissive": "#rrggbb", "opacity", "segments"}. Units are metres and y is up; put the model's base at y = 0 so it stands on the ground. Wedge is a ramp sloping down toward +z. Torus lies flat; size [outer width, tube thickness, outer depth]. /*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.

 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),

 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

kit3d.js API:
/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)

 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by

 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *

 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.
 */

 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';

 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)

 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).

 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

/*
 * kit3d.js: a small, tested 3D game engine on three.js from Freehand's game kit.
 * game.js is a module that starts with:  import { Kit, THREE } from './kit3d.js';
 *
 *   Kit.start({ init, update, title, hint, camera, sky, debug })
 *     init(g)        build a round: the world and g.player. Runs on every start and restart; everything
 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *
 * Every object stands on its position: y is the BOTTOM of the shape, so y = 0 sits on the ground.
 * Models face +z (make_model models do too).
 *   Kit.box(w, h, d, color, x, y, z)   Kit.sphere(r, color, x, y, z)   Kit.cylinder(r, h, color, x, y, z)
 *   Kit.cone(r, h, color, x, y, z)     Kit.gem(r, color, x, y, z)      Kit.ring(r, thick, color, x, y, z) (y = centre)
 *   Kit.group(x, y, z)   Kit.ground(size, color, color2)   Kit.add(obj)   Kit.remove(obj)
 *   Kit.model('assets/player.glb', fallback)  shows fallback (a shape) until the file loads; Kit.anim(obj, 'Run') plays an animation
 *   Kit.walk(obj, amount)  swings parts named leg/arm while moving (amount 0..1)
 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.
 * Physics: Kit.solid(obj, moving) makes obj a wall or platform. Kit.move(obj, dt, {gravity, floor}) moves obj by
 *   obj.vel (a THREE.Vector3), adds gravity, stops at solids and at the floor (y = 0; floor: null for none).
 *   After it: obj.onGround, obj.hitWall. obj.size = {w, h, d} sets the body size (default 0.8 x 1.7 x 0.8).
 * Kit.camera and Kit.scene are the three.js camera and scene (Kit.camera.add(gun) puts a gun in view). Kit.sun and Kit.hemi are the lights.
 * Kit.hit(a, b) boxes touch   Kit.near(a, b, dist)   Kit.aim(list) first object in list under the screen centre
 * Kit.addScore(n), Kit.hud('Lives 3') (Kit.hud('Time 30', 'timer') adds a second line), Kit.sfx('jump' | 'coin' | 'hit' | 'boom' | 'power' | 'click' | 'shoot'),
 * Kit.burst(position, color), Kit.shake(amount), Kit.rand(a, b), Kit.clamp(v, lo, hi)
 *
 * The state is mirrored to window.__game (with the player's position) so play_test can report it.

 *                    made with Kit helpers is removed first, so build it all again here.
 *     update(g, dt)  move things; dt is in seconds. Kit.gameOver() (or Kit.gameOver('You win!')) ends the round.
 *     camera         'third'  behind and above g.player; Q/E or dragging the mouse turns it
 *                    'chase'  behind the way g.player faces (cars, planes, runners)
 *                    'first'  from g.player's eyes; the mouse looks (click locks it), arrows/Q/E turn
 *                    'top'    high above g.player, looking down
 *                    'fixed'  you place g.camera yourself
 *   g.player         set it in init. The camera follows it and play_test reports where it is.
 *

 *   Kit.face(obj, dir, dt) turns obj smoothly toward the direction {x, z}
 * Input: Kit.down('left') held, Kit.pressed('jump') this frame only. Actions: left right up down jump action run.
 *   Other keys by code: Kit.key('KeyB') pressed this frame, Kit.keyDown('KeyC') held (KeyA..KeyZ, Digit1..Digit9, Tab).
 *   Space = jump; click, Enter, F, X or Z = action. Kit.moveInput() = {x, z} from WASD/arrows, relative to the camera.

function.name: make_sprite
function.description: Draw pixel-art and save it as a PNG for a 2D game. "pixels" is a list of strings, one per row; each character is one pixel and "." is transparent. "palette" maps each character to a color ("#rrggbb" or a name like red, yellow). "scale" makes each pixel bigger (default 4). For animation give "frames" (a list of pixel lists, same size) to get a sprite sheet with frames side by side. Example bird 8x6: {"path":"assets/bird.png","pixels":["..YYYY..",".YYYYWB.","YYYYYYOO","OYYYYYY.",".YYYYY..","..Y..Y.."],"palette":{"Y":"#ffd23f","W":"white","B":"black","O":"orange"}}. Draw it with Kit.image("assets/bird.png") and Kit.drawImage.

frames.description: several pixel grids for an animation sheet

function.name: make_model
function.description: Build a low-poly 3D model (.glb, loads with three.js GLTFLoader) out of simple shapes. Shapes: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, wedge, torus. Each part: {"shape", "size": [width, height, depth] (the box the shape fills), "position": [x, y, z] (its centre), "on": "<name of an earlier part>" to rest it on top of that part (then x and z are offsets from that part's centre and y is ignored), "rotation": [x, y, z] degrees, "color": "#rrggbb", optional "name", "flat": true for a faceted look, "roughness", "metalness", "emissive": "#rrggbb", "opacity", "segments"}. Units are metres and y is up; put the model's base at y = 0 so it stands on the ground. Wedge is a ramp sloping down toward +z. Torus lies flat; size [outer width, tube thickness, outer depth]. function.name: game_recipe
function.description: Tested code to add a feature to a kit.js or kit3d.js game, in parts (top of game.js, init, update, and draw for 2D) to paste in with file_edit. It picks the 2D or 3D version for the game in the workspace. 2D recipes: "lives" (three lives with a short invincible blink after each hit, hearts drawn in the corner); "coins" (coins that appear around the level and score when the player touches them); "powerup" (a shield power-up that floats in now and then; touching it makes the player safe for 5 seconds); "sprite" (draw the player from a PNG made with make_sprite, with a walking or flapping animation from a sprite sheet); "chaser" (enemies that appear at the edges and move toward the player; touching one ends the round (or calls hurt() from the lives recipe)); "timer" (a countdown; when it reaches zero the round ends with "Time up!" and the score stays); "levels" (a level number that goes up every 10 points, makes things faster and shows a "Level N" banner); "background" (a scrolling starfield or snowfall behind everything (draw it first in draw())). 3D recipes: "lives" (three lives with a blinking safe time after each hit; call hurt() where the game used to end the round); "coins" (spinning coins around the player that score when touched; new ones keep appearing); "chaser" (enemies (assets/enemy.glb, a red ball until it exists) that appear around the player and chase it; touching one calls hurt() from the lives recipe, or ends the round); "shooting" (click, Enter or F fires balls the way the player faces; they defeat chasers (from the chaser recipe) and score); "moving_platforms" (platforms that slide and bob; the player rides them (they are solid)); "timer" (a countdown on screen; at zero the round ends with "Time up!" and the score stays); "powerup" (a speed-boost gem appears now and then; touching it makes boostTime > 0 for 5 seconds (multiply the speed by boostTime > 0 ? 1.8 : 1)); "levels" (a level number that goes up every 10 points with a sound; multiply speeds by levelSpeed() to make it harder); "scenery" (copies of a model made with make_model (trees, houses, rocks) placed around the world as solid scenery); "gather" (survival gathering: trees and rocks around the world; press F, Enter or click next to one to hit it for wood or stone, shown in an inventory line (inv.wood, inv.stone)); "craft" (crafting for the gather recipe: press 1 for a hatchet (5 wood, doubles wood) and 2 for a pickaxe (3 wood + 5 stone, doubles stone); a line shows the recipes and what you have); "build" (building for the gather recipe: press B to place a wooden wall in front of the player (2 wood) and V for a stone one (2 stone); walls are solid); "hunger" (survival needs: health and hunger that run down; berry bushes to eat from (F, Enter or click next to one); starving hurts and at 0 health the round ends); "daynight" (a day and night cycle (one day is 90 seconds): the sky and lights darken at night; g.night is true at night, so other code can spawn more enemies then).

function.name: make_sprite
function.description: Draw pixel-art and save it as a PNG for a 2D game. "pixels" is a list of strings, one per row; each character is one pixel and "." is transparent. "palette" maps each character to a color ("#rrggbb" or a name like red, yellow). "scale" makes each pixel bigger (default 4). For animation give "frames" (a list of pixel lists, same size) to get a sprite sheet with frames side by side. Example bird 8x6: {"path":"assets/bird.png","pixels":["..YYYY..",".YYYYWB.","YYYYYYOO","OYYYYYY.",".YYYYY..","..Y..Y.."],"palette":{"Y":"#ffd23f","W":"white","B":"black","O":"orange"}}. Draw it with Kit.image("assets/bird.png") and Kit.drawImage.

frames.description: several pixel grids for an animation sheet

function.name: make_model
function.description: Build a low-poly 3D model (.glb, loads with three.js GLTFLoader) out of simple shapes. Shapes: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, wedge, torus. Each part: {"shape", "size": [width, height, depth] (the box the shape fills), "position": [x, y, z] (its centre), "on": "<name of an earlier part>" to rest it on top of that part (then x and z are offsets from that part's centre and y is ignored), "rotation": [x, y, z] degrees, "color": "#rrggbb", optional "name", "flat": true for a faceted look, "roughness", "metalness", "emissive": "#rrggbb", "opacity", "segments"}. Units are metres and y is up; put the model's base at y = 0 so it stands on the ground. Wedge is a ramp sloping down toward +z. Torus lies flat; size [outer width, tube thickness, outer depth]. Example: a tree is a "cylinder" trunk {"size":[0.3,1.2,0.3],"position":[0,0.6,0],"color":"#8b5a2b"} and a "cone" top {"size":[1.4,1.8,1.4],"position":[0,2.1,0],"color":"#3f8f3a","flat":true,"segments":7}.

parts.description: the shapes that make up the model

function.name: file_write
function.description: Create or overwrite a file in the workspace (parent folders are created). Use this for deliverables: reports, code, CSV, HTML.

function.name: file_edit
function.description: Replace one exact piece of text in a workspace file. "find" must match exactly once.

function.name: shell
function.description: Run a shell command in the workspace folder (sh). Use for installing packages, running scripts, git, downloads. Output is capped; long-running servers will time out.

function.name: python
function.description: Run a Python 3 script (saved and executed in the workspace). Print results to stdout. Good for data processing, charts (matplotlib if installed), converting files.

function.name: play_test
function.description: Run a game or web page from the workspace in a real browser and test it like a player. Returns uncaught errors, console errors, files that failed to load, visible text and a screenshot. Optional "actions" are inputs played in order: "click" (centre), "click X Y", "click Start Game" (a button by its text), "click #start" (CSS selector), "key ArrowLeft 500" (hold ms), "key Space", "tap Space 8 350" (8 quick presses 350 ms apart, for flapping or jumping games), "type hello", "mouse X Y", "wait 1000". After each input it says whether the screen changed, and it reports window.__game (state and score) for games built on the game kit. "Errors: none" does not mean the game works: read "What happened" and WATCH OUT. Run it after every change to a game and fix everything it reports. The user can play the same file in the Play tab.

path.description: HTML file in the workspace, default index.html

actions.description: inputs to play, e.g. ["click", "key ArrowRight 800", "key Space"]

seconds.description: extra seconds to let it run before the screenshot, default 3

function.name: game_engine
function.description: Set up a new game you will write yourself: copies index.html and the game engine (kit.js for 2D, kit3d.js for 3D). The engine handles the loop, input, camera, physics, sounds and the title and game-over screens; there is no game yet. Then write game.js yourself with file_write: the world, the player, the rules, the goal.

title.description: game title shown on the title screen

function.name: game_template
function.description: Copy a finished starter game. Only use it when the user asks to start from a template or starter; otherwise write the game yourself with game_engine. Templates: "flyer" (tap/Space to flap through gaps between obstacles (gravity, scrolling pipes or walls, score per gap passed)); "platformer" (side-scrolling run and jump: tile level, coins, stompable enemies, a goal flag); "topdown" (move in 8 directions, collect items, dodge enemies that chase you, waves get harder); "snake" (grid snake: arrow keys steer, eat food to grow, walls and your own tail end the round); "breakout" (paddle and ball (arrow keys or mouse) breaking rows of bricks, 3 lives, win by clearing them); "shooter" (vertical space shooter: move left and right, hold Space to fire at enemies falling from the top, 3 lives); "runner" (endless runner: the hero runs by itself, Space jumps (double jump) over obstacles, speeds up over time); "blank" (empty kit.js game (a box that moves) for any other 2D game: puzzles, card games, rhythm, racing); "3d" (3D third-person adventure: walk and jump around an island, collect gems, slimes chase you, 3 lives); "3d-platformer" (3D platformer: jump across floating and moving platforms, collect coins, reach the flag, falling costs a life); "3d-fps" (3D first-person shooter: arena with walls, mouse/arrow look, click or Enter to shoot enemies that come in waves, health); "3d-racer" (3D racing: drive a car round a track through checkpoints, 3 laps against the clock, cones to avoid, off-road is slow); "3d-runner" (3D endless runner: 3 lanes, left/right to switch lanes, Space jumps barriers, dodge walls, collect coins, speeds up); "3d-flyer" (3D flying: a plane flies forward, arrows steer, fly through rings for points, dodge floating rocks, 3 lives); "3d-blank" (empty kit3d.js game (a character that walks and jumps on a ground) for any other 3D game).
